title: N4 · Unit 7

lesson.title: Dinner at the Yamamotos'
lesson.description: Visit an older host, recognise respectful language, thank people appropriately and separate expectation from confirmation.
lesson.canDo: Choose wording appropriate to a host and identify the arrangements in a thank-you message

grammar.title: Respect the person doing the action
grammar.formation: 行く/来る/いる → いらっしゃる; 食べる/飲む → 召し上がる; 言う → おっしゃる; 見る → ご覧になる; する → なさる; くれる → くださる. Special polite stems: いらっしゃいます・おっしゃいます・なさいます・くださいます.
grammar.explanation: Honorific verbs raise the person whose action you describe; they do not raise yourself. Use 先生はいらっしゃいます for the teacher's presence, and 私はいます for your own. Honorific vocabulary and です/ます politeness are different: one concerns the actor, the other the listener. Everyday polite verbs remain acceptable in many situations; use the precise honorific target when the task explicitly asks for it.
grammar.example: 先生は何とおっしゃいましたか。

examples.ja: お{茶|ちゃ}を{召|め}し{上|あ}がりますか。
{先生|せんせい}は{写真|しゃしん}をご{覧|らん}になりました。
examples.en: The teacher looked at the photographs.

examples.ja: {山本|やまもと}さんはいらっしゃいますか。

grammar.mistake: Do not describe yourself with 私はいらっしゃいます. いらっしゃいます has the special い stem, not いらっしゃります.

grammar.title: A respectful action or request
grammar.formation: お + native verb ます-stem + になる (読む → お読みになる). Respectful request: お + stem + ください. Some actions use a special verb instead.
grammar.explanation: お読みになる describes a respected person's reading. お読みください requests that action respectfully. Do not stack both constructions or apply お～になる blindly to する compounds. This unit practises common native-verb patterns; compound-specific ご～ forms will receive their own examples later.
grammar.example: こちらをお読みください。

examples.ja: {先生|せんせい}はお{帰|かえ}りになりました。
こちらでお{待|ま}ちください。
このお{知|し}らせをお{読|よ}みになりますか。

grammar.mistake: Use お読みになります, not お読むになります. お読みください is a request, not a statement that the action happened.

grammar.title: Thank someone; evaluate an outcome; explain an expectation
grammar.formation: Verb て-form + くれてありがとう (close relationship); ～てくださってありがとうございます (respectful). Verb て-form + よかったです. Plain verb/い-adjective + はず; noun + のはず; な-adjective + なはず.
grammar.explanation: Thank a friend with 手伝ってくれてありがとう; thank an older host respectfully with 迎えてくださってありがとうございます. ～てよかった evaluates an action or outcome positively after the fact. ～はず expresses an expectation based on grounds, not certainty and not the obligation of 'should do'. Say what supports the expectation and check it when necessary.

examples.ja: {準備|じゅんび}を{手伝|てつだ}ってくれてありがとう。
examples.en: Thank you for helping me prepare (to a friend).

examples.ja: {迎|むか}えてくださって、ありがとうございます。
examples.en: Thank you for meeting me on arrival (respectful).

examples.ja: {六時|ろくじ}に{戻|もど}るはずですが、まだ{確認|かくにん}していません。
examples.en: I expect them back at six, but I haven't checked yet.

grammar.mistake: 戻るはず is an expectation; 戻った says it happened. Advice to return is not 戻るはず. Use ご主人 for someone else's husband, not as a requirement to describe every family's structure.

dialogues.title: An invitation to dinner
dialogues.scene: You and Hana visit Yamamoto-san, an older host. You ask about her husband's expected return; the arrival is not yet confirmed.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: {迎|むか}えてくださって、ありがとうございます。{失礼|しつれい}します。
lines.romaji: Mukaete kudasatte, arigatō gozaimasu. Shitsurei shimasu.
lines.meaning: Thank you for meeting us. Excuse me as I come in.

lines.speaker: Yamamoto
lines.line: よくいらっしゃいました。どうぞ、お{入|はい}りください。

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: ご{主人|しゅじん}はいらっしゃいますか。

lines.speaker: Yamamoto
lines.line: {六時|ろくじ}に{戻|もど}るはずですが、まだ{確認|かくにん}していません。
lines.romaji: Rokuji ni modoru hazu desu ga, mada kakunin shite imasen.
lines.meaning: I expect him back at six, but I haven't checked yet.

lines.speaker: Hana
lines.line: {鍵|かぎ}は{見|み}つかりました。{交番|こうばん}で{受|う}け{取|と}ってから{来|き}ました。
lines.romaji: Kagi wa mitsukarimashita. Kōban de uketotte kara kimashita.
lines.meaning: The key was found. We came after collecting it at the police box.

lines.speaker: Yamamoto
lines.line: それはよかったですね。お{茶|ちゃ}を{召|め}し{上|あ}がりますか。
lines.romaji: Sore wa yokatta desu ne. Ocha o meshiagarimasu ka.
lines.meaning: That's good to hear. Would you like some tea?

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: はい、ありがとうございます。{後|あと}で{大学|だいがく}のことで{質問|しつもん}してもいいですか。
lines.romaji: Hai, arigatō gozaimasu. Ato de daigaku no koto de shitsumon shite mo ii desu ka.
lines.meaning: Yes, thank you. May I ask about university later?

dialogues.title: After the meal
dialogues.scene: You thank the host after dinner. Hana is a close friend who helped prepare the visit, so she receives a different level of thanks.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: {夕食|ゆうしょく}、とてもおいしかったです。ごちそうさまでした。
lines.romaji: Yūshoku, totemo oishikatta desu. Gochisōsama deshita.
lines.meaning: Dinner was delicious. Thank you for the meal.

lines.speaker: Yamamoto
lines.line: {来|き}てくださって、ありがとうございます。お{土産|みやげ}も、うれしいです。
lines.romaji: Kite kudasatte, arigatō gozaimasu. Omiyage mo, ureshii desu.
lines.meaning: Thank you for coming. I'm pleased about the gift too.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: {来|き}てよかったです。ご{家族|かぞく}にもよろしくお{伝|つた}えください。
lines.romaji: Kite yokatta desu. Gokazoku ni mo yoroshiku otsutae kudasai.
lines.meaning: I'm glad I came. Please give my regards to your family too.

lines.speaker: Hana
lines.line: {天気|てんき}{予報|よほう}では、{夜|よる}は{雨|あめ}だそうです。{急|いそ}ぎましょう。
lines.romaji: Tenki yohō de wa, yoru wa ame da sō desu. Isogimashō.
lines.meaning: The forecast says it will rain at night. Let's hurry.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: ハナさん、{準備|じゅんび}を{手伝|てつだ}ってくれてありがとう。
lines.romaji: Hana-san, junbi o tetsudatte kurete arigatō.
lines.meaning: Hana, thank you for helping me prepare.

lines.speaker: Hana
lines.line: こちらこそ。{明日|あした}、お{礼|れい}のメールを{書|か}こう。
lines.romaji: Kochira koso. Ashita, orei no mēru o kakō.
lines.meaning: Thank you too. Let's write a thank-you email tomorrow.

exercises.prompt: Has the host confirmed her husband's return time?
options: No; six is her expectation, still unchecked
Yes; he called to confirm six
Yes; he is already sitting at dinner
exercises.explain: 戻るはずですが、まだ確認していません explicitly separates expectation from confirmation.

exercises.prompt: Where was the key collected before the visit?
exercises.explain: Hana says 交番で受け取ってから来ました.

exercises.prompt: What reason does Hana give for hurrying?
options: Rain is forecast for the night
exercises.explain: Hana cites the forecast before proposing 急ぎましょう.
You thank Hana directly for helping with preparation.

exercises.context: Ask respectfully whether your teacher is present. Use the special honorific verb.
exercises.explain: いる becomes いらっしゃる, with the special polite form いらっしゃいます.

exercises.context: State respectfully that the teacher read the notice.
exercises.line: {先生|せんせい}はお{知|し}らせをお{読|よ}み＿＿。
exercises.explain: お + 読み + になる respects the teacher's action. This is a statement, not a request.

exercises.context: You are thanking an older host politely for meeting you at the station. Choose the respectful thanks practised here.
exercises.prompt: Which wording fits this host relationship?
options: {迎|むか}えてくださって、ありがとうございます。
{迎|むか}えてくれてありがとう。
exercises.explain: てくださってありがとうございます thanks the respected helper. The middle option is casual friend-level thanks; the last describes your giving a favour.

exercises.context: Hana is your close friend. Thank her in casual style for helping prepare, as requested by this task.
exercises.prompt: Which is casual thanks to the friend?
options: {準備|じゅんび}を{手伝|てつだ}ってくれてありがとう。
{準備|じゅんび}を{手伝|てつだ}ってくださいました。
{準備|じゅんび}を{手伝|てつだ}ってあげる。
exercises.explain: くれてありがとう directly thanks the friend. くださいました reports completed respectful help but does not itself say thanks.

exercises.line: お{茶|ちゃ}を{召|め}し{上|あ}がりますか。
exercises.context: Accept the host's offer politely, speaking about your own action without raising yourself.
options: はい、ありがとうございます。
はい、{私|わたし}が{召|め}し{上|あ}がります。
{先生|せんせい}はいらっしゃいます。
exercises.explain: The first reply accepts without self-honorification. 召し上がる is for the respected other person's action.

exercises.line: {鍵|かぎ}は{見|み}つかりましたか。
exercises.context: You have collected it and are glad you checked at the police box. State that positive completed result.
options: はい。{交番|こうばん}で{確認|かくにん}してよかったです。
まだ{探|さが}しています。
{見|み}つかるはずですが、まだわかりません。
exercises.explain: てよかった evaluates the completed checking positively; the other replies leave the search uncertain.

exercises.meaning: Please convey my thanks to your family (respectful).
exercises.explain: お + 伝え + ください makes the respectful request; the family is the に-marked recipient.

exercises.context: Based on yesterday's message, you expect the host back at six, but have not checked today's arrival.
exercises.line: {六時|ろくじ}に{戻|もど}る＿＿です。
exercises.explain: A plain verb connects directly to はず. The expectation is not a confirmed arrival.

exercises.prompt: What will the writer bring on Friday?
exercises.explain: そのお知らせ refers to the university notice the host wanted to read.

options: The writer will send an email
The writer will change the class time
The host will collect a key
exercises.explain: 出発する前に、メールで連絡します gives the planned contact before departure.

exercises.prompt: Whose photographs did the host show?
exercises.explain: ご家族の写真 identifies the host's family.

exercises.prompt: What additional action is requested at the end?
options: Convey thanks to the host's husband
exercises.explain: ご主人にもお礼をお伝えください requests conveying thanks; no return time is confirmed by this email.

watch.prompt: Optionally save up to five lines showing whom a speaker respects or what they expect. Separate respect for an actor from politeness to the listener. Do not copy fictional role-language as everyday etiquette.
